The finite-rank term defines part of the prior itself rather than approximating a different dense covariance.

method_specification.kernel_adaptation_s.reason: The paper specifies chordal distances, periodic length-scale fields, the product Wendland term, normalized Fourier weights, all one- and two-body terms, and truncations M1=10 and M2=3 giving rank 661. kernel_contribution.kernel_differs_from_.reason: The construction meaningfully extends the reference family through a per-circle periodic product support and a global one-/two-body Fourier covariance with an exact rank-661 representation. kernel_contribution.existing_kernel_inad.reason: At the common training size and test set, the existing-kernel runs obtain CRPS 2.57428, 2.57243, and 2.56330, versus 2.38294 for TAW. kernel_contribution.adaptation_motivated.reason: Angular periodicity motivates chordal geometry and seam-free support; molecular torsional expansions motivate global Fourier one- and two-body terms. The local component addresses finer structure while the decomposition preserves computational feasibility.

kernel_contribution.domain_warrants_new_.reason: The input space is a product of circles with coupled molecular torsions and a rough relaxed energy surface. Geometry, interaction structure, and local-support volume affect prediction and full-scale covariance feasibility; this is not a trivially smooth Euclidean benchmark.

insight_contribution.insight_present.reason: The paper develops nontrivial observations about weak surviving local covariances, the fitted distribution of torsion-coupling amplitudes, seam-induced uncertainty, and regional miscalibration. These go beyond reporting a baseline win, although some stronger interpretations are unsupported.

insight_contribution.insight_grounded_in.reason: Sparsity, fitted amplitudes, and regional residual claims have concrete artifacts. The proposed localization of irreproducible scans is also not demonstrated.
